findings: A pear-shaped preserved coalified flower body with a broken basal stump, twelve fused carpels and twelve outward-bending free apical tips surrounding one short central column.
Only ten elliptical outer bases/scars and twenty smaller rhombic stamen bases; one outer scar may represent a bract. No complete tepal, petal, stamen or external ovule is reconstructed.
Paired low inner ventral crests at each free carpel tip. A physical ENLARGED label makes the interpretive educational scale explicit.
facts.limits: Single holotype S122015 of Friis et al.2009; preserved organ only, not a living water lily. Three-dimensional missing backs, relief, palette and enlarged display dimensions are interpretive, not an exact cast or measured scaling. Outer organ phyllotaxis is unresolved; minor irregularity avoids asserting a neat living spiral/whorl.
facts.concept_corrections: Original ImageGen inspected. Retain fossil-only pear body and radial opening. Shorten the generated tall, flame-like free carpel tips and central column; enforce exactly twelve tips and subtle short scar bases. No complete petals. Concept cannot establish counts or fossil truth.

findings: One slender short fruiting axis bears six spaced cymules, each supporting TWO separate fruits on short pedicels: twelve visible nutlets total.

Each oval slightly flattened nutlet has TWO equal opposite bracts; EACH bract is deeply bilobed with a few irregular pointed teeth. Twenty-four bilobed bracts total; their deep sinuses are silhouette geometry.

Nutlets have subtle longitudinal ridges and small bifurcate styles. Expose nut fronts and short attachments between the open paired bracts. No tree, leaves, pollen, staminate catkin, rock slab or parent shoot connection.
facts.limits: Select P.joffrensis Sun & Stockey1992, holotype S26016 A/B and original Figs1-16, especially4,6,11,15-16. This is one generalized fruiting organ, not a whole tree. Counts, three-dimensional cymule spacing and fossil palette are artistic; fossil bracts vary considerably. Reported nutlet3-6x2-3.5mm and bract6-12mm lengths guide nominal design, not new microscopic hard gates.
facts.concept_corrections: ImageGen inspected. Its single alternating fruits fail the intended paired cymules, and cup-like bracts are not each deeply bilobed. Correct final geometry to six two-fruit cymules, two equal individually bilobed bracts per fruit and exposed nutlets. Retain color restraint and small open axis, not the incorrect concept counts.

findings: A labeled enlarged educational thallus relief on a simple thin neutral tablet. One main uniseriate axis bears five asymmetrically placed lateral branches, two of those branch again. Laterals emerge below septal constrictions, turn upward, and do not form a repetitive dichotomous Y tree.

Sparse shallow septal constrictions, mostly elongate cylinders, modest distal widening and one subtle club/cup-shaped external cell outline. Narrow apical extensions on selected tips; tiny lobate/subdiscoidal holdfast.
No fronds, leaf blades, roots, berries, coral polyps, giant hollow goblets, microscopic pores or cell-wall texture. The mounted relief is real closed volume, not an alpha decal.
facts.limits: Tang et al.2020 P.antiquus, Fig1 and Fig2 original fossil images and original diagnosis read. Actual thalli0.3-3.3mm long. Enlarged display dimensions, exact topology, selected cell boundaries and tablet are interpretive, not a fossil cast or quantitative cell measurement. About1billion years old near latest Mesoproterozoic/early Tonian boundary, not falsely exact Neoproterozoic dating.
facts.concept_corrections: ImageGen inspected. Preserve negative spaces and asymmetric upward lateral pattern but reject the exaggerated hollow goblet, teardrop pods, woody knuckles and rough stone texture. Final geometry uses thin mostly cylindrical filaments with gentle widening and connected shallow constrictions, ensuring multiorder topology is readable at512px.

findings: One conservative complete vegetative module: short horizontal rhizome with three modest roots, upright slender stem, upper floating rosette and four filiform submerged leaves. No flowers or fruits are invented.

Upper rosette has four compound leaves in opposite pairs, each with four leaflet pairs and one terminal leaflet. Four small simple leaves occupy the center as two opposite pairs. Forty ovate/obovate toothed blades total, with open visible petiole/rachis connections.

Submerged leaves divide dichotomously through three levels into slender filiform segments, clearly distinct from the floating toothed blades. Root laterals are sparse, not an elaborate generic aquarium root mass.
facts.limits: Family incertae sedis; Trapago is an illegitimate junior synonym, not another asset. Liang2021 provides directly inspected original text and fossil Fig2 A,C,D,E for floating/compound and submerged foliage. Stockey & Rothwell1997 original published abstract supports rhizome, root and opposite simple/compound arrangement, but its historic separate-genera view is superseded by Hickey nomenclature as discussed by Liang2021. Choose a generalized vegetative module, not an exact one-specimen whole plant; colors, thicknesses, attachment angles and all absolute display dimensions are nominal artistic choices. No modern Trapa nut.
facts.concept_corrections: ImageGen inspected. Retain upper compound rosette/lower fine-fan contrast and rhizome. Correct lower fans into genuine iterative dichotomy rather than a central feather rachis; enforce four nine-leaflet compound leaves plus four simple leaves and visible attachment gaps. Reduce woody thickness and roots. No giant unlobed lily pads.
